issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the experiments 'support the theoretical findings'. The theorems of Section 3 assume a globally Lipschitz nonlinearity and analyze the Section 2 residuals (per-direction Laplacian weights, weighted boundary time-derivative and, for the wave, endpoint-gradient terms, plus the neural-residual penalty). The experiments use v(u)=-u+u^2, which the paper itself states is only locally Lipschitz with theoretical convergence 'open', and the implemented losses (eq:lossheat, eq:losswave) weight the Laplacian as a single term, omit the boundary time-derivative weighting and the wave endpoint-gradient terms. Thus the experiments neither satisfy the theorems' hypotheses nor implement the analyzed loss, so the claimed support is not established by the source.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In this case, the WeightedPINN loss reduces to the standard PINN loss.

issues.failure_explanation: In eq:barRG1 (and barRG2-barRG4) the tilde-weighted boundary terms are d copies of the plain L2 trace of u_theta (no derivatives), while the 2D illustrations weight the full spatial derivatives ∂_{x_i}u_θ on Σ_T, and the standard residual uses the tangential Sobolev norm ‖u_θ‖_{H1(Σ_T)}. These are mutually incompatible. As defined, the weighted boundary residual controls strictly less than the standard one (no derivative of the trace), so the Remark that at φ≡1 'the WeightedPINN loss reduces to the standard PINN loss' is false under eq:barRG1. Conversely, the illustrated version penalizes ∂_{x_i}u_θ, which for the exact solution is generally nonzero on Σ_T (it equals ν_i ∂_νu since u=0 only forces tangential derivatives to vanish), so the illustrated loss does not vanish at the exact solution. There is a genuine choice between mathematically different repairs (plain trace, full gradient, tangential gradient), and the choice changes what the method's loss controls.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the tilde-weight terms consistently (e.g., on tangential gradient components of the trace, matching the H1(Σ_T) structure of the standard residual), and correct the Section 2.3 illustrations and the Remark accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The WeightedPINN boundary formulation is not well defined; all results stated in terms of the residuals eq:barRG1-eq:barRG4 refer to an ambiguous object, and the claim that the formulation 'extends naturally' the standard boundary treatment is unsupported.
issues.title: Inconsistent definition of the weighted boundary residual: the tilde-weight terms contradict the 2D illustrations and weaken the standard H1 boundary control
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition of four displayed residuals plus matching fixes to the illustration and Remark preserves every substantive claim and guarantee; no theorem's intended content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the weighted residual gives R̄_Q^1(u_ε,f_ε) = R̄_Q^1(u,f) + O(‖û‖+‖f̂‖), where R̄_Q^1(u,f) = (φ_{θ^1}-1)∂_t u - Σ(φ_{θ̄^i}-1)∂_{x_i x_i}u + (φ_{θ^2}-1)v(u) - (φ_{θ^3}-1)f1_ω. This weight-deviation term vanishes only when all weights are identically 1, but the theorem asserts its conclusion for arbitrary fixed weight parameters (Assumption A2 only requires boundedness). The same omission occurs in the boundary estimate: ‖φ_{θ^6}(0)u_θ(0)-φ_{θ^7}(0)u_0‖ contains the uncontrolled deviation (φ_{θ^6}(0)-φ_{θ^7}(0))u_0. Hence the proof establishes only the trivial weights≡1 case (standard PINN), where the WeightedPINN content disappears; for general weights the claim is unsupported and fails in regimes such as a vanishing control weight φ_{θ^3}≡0 with small ρ, where the equation residual contains no control term and the loss has a positive infimum for data the free dynamics cannot connect. Also, since the networks may depend on the fixed weight configuration, no bound on the min-max value of the Section 2 formulation follows. The identical defect is replicated in the proofs of thm:errorWave, thm:errorHeatb and thm:errorWaveb.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either restrict the theorems to weights≡1 (reducing them to standard PINN approximation and abandoning the advertised regime) or prove residual smallness for arbitrary bounded weights, which requires establishing controllability/approximability for all weight-perturbed equations - essentially new proof architecture.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central approximation guarantees for WeightedPINNs (Theorems on smallness of the weighted loss) are unestablished outside the weights≡1 case; the min-max training objective of Section 2 receives no valid guarantee.
issues.title: Approximation theorems: the key residual estimates omit the weight-deviation terms and are valid only for weights identically one
issues.why_classification: The only regime the proof handles is the one in which the method coincides with standard PINNs, so the advertised guarantee (arbitrary adaptive weights) is lost; every supported resolution either excludes the advertised regime or requires new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, \(f-f_{\bar{\theta}}\) is the exact control with corresponding weak solution \(\tilde u\) of the equation

issues.failure_explanation: The conclusion bounds the distance to a pre-designated pair (u,f), but the loss is zero at every exact control pair, and exact pairs are non-unique: for v≡0 with zero data, any ψ ∈ C_c^∞((0,T)×ω), ψ≠0, yields a second exact pair (ψ, (∂_t-Δ)ψ) with ψ(0)=ψ(T)=0, distinct from the designated (0,0). Networks approximating this second pair make the loss (in particular its value at weights≡1) arbitrarily small - so the hypothesis holds with δ→0 - while ‖f-f_θ̄‖ stays near ‖(∂_t-Δ)ψ‖ > 0, contradicting the conclusion. The corresponding invalid proof step is eq:f_est1, which applies the controllability estimate of [fernandez-cara_guerrero_2006, Theorem 1.6] to the arbitrary control difference f-f_θ̄; such a norm bound cannot hold for an arbitrary control driving ũ(0) to zero, precisely because zero-effect controls exist.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reformulate the conclusion (e.g., closeness to some exact control pair, or to a minimal-norm control) and replace the misapplied controllability estimate by a valid argument; the guarantee type necessarily changes.
issues.overall_effect: The stated stability guarantee for the heat equation (small weighted loss implies closeness to the designated solution and control, with C depending only on Q_T, v, λ) is false, including its standard-PINN special case; the 'converse' reading of the convergence analysis in Section 3 is unreliable.
issues.title: Heat stability theorem is false: a small loss does not imply closeness to the designated control (exact controls are non-unique)
issues.why_classification: The primary claim is false as stated (an explicit in-source counterexample exists via zero-effect controls), and any repair changes the central quantifier/guarantee from closeness to the designated control to closeness to an unspecified or minimal control.

issues.failure_explanation: ū is defined as the weak solution of the semilinear heat equation with source f_θ̄1_ω and terminal condition ū(T)=z₀, i.e., a final-value (backward-in-time) parabolic problem. Such problems are ill-posed: in the linear case a solution exists only if z₀ - ∫S(T-s)f_θ̄1_ω ds lies in the domain of the unbounded operator S(T)^{-1} (exponentially decaying spectral coefficients), a meager subspace of L²; for generic z₀ ∈ L² and generic network output f_θ̄ no such ū exists. The cited references concern forward initial-value well-posedness and cannot yield backward existence. The proof's central comparison object is therefore generally undefined.

failure_location.quote: It follows from the approach developed in \cite{Cazenave1980} (see also \cite[Equation (1.4)]{FernandezZuazua2000}) that the above semilinear heat equation admits a unique solution. Consequently, \(\bar u\) is well defined.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the backward construction of ū by a legitimate argument (e.g., observability/Carleman estimates applied directly to the residual equation for u-u_θ), which is a different proof architecture unavailable in the source.
issues.overall_effect: The entire chain of estimates in the proof of Theorem thm:error_estHeat (the equations for û, the energy estimate, eq:f_est1, eq:tilde_u_est1 and the final combination) rests on an object that generally does not exist, so the proof collapses independently of other defects.
issues.title: Heat stability proof constructs the comparison solution ū via an ill-posed final-value (backward) heat problem
issues.why_classification: Backward solvability is unavailable in principle for parabolic problems, so any correct proof of a comparable stability statement for the heat equation requires essentially new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: Integration by parts produces the boundary term -∫_{∂Ω} û ∂_νû dx = -∫_{∂Ω} u_θ(∂_νu_θ - ∂_νū) dx, since û = u_θ on Σ_T while ū = 0 there only forces tangential derivatives of ū to vanish, not ∂_νū. The written identity drops the term -∫u_θ∂_νū involving the uncontrolled normal derivative of ū. Moreover, the retained part is bounded via ‖u_θ‖²_{H¹(∂Ω)}, but the normal derivative ∂_νu_θ is not part of the tangential H¹(∂Ω) norm, so the inequality ‖∇u_θ·ν‖_{L²(∂Ω)} ≤ ‖u_θ‖_{H¹(∂Ω)} is false; and the hypothesis's weighted boundary residual controls only L² norms of u_θ and ∂_tu_θ on Σ_T, so no available quantity controls ∂_νu_θ. Additionally, ‖û‖²_{H¹(Ω)} is placed on the left of eq:energy although û has nonvanishing boundary trace, so Poincaré does not apply. The energy estimate and eq:hat_u_est1 are therefore unproven.

issues.failure_explanation: With d=10, the removed closed ball B((1/d,...,1/d), 3/4) has center at distance 1/√10 ≈ 0.316 from the origin and thus reaches distance 0.316+0.75 ≈ 1.066 > 1; in particular the boundary point c/|c| of the unit ball lies at distance 1-1/√10 ≈ 0.684 < 0.75 from the center and is therefore inside the removed ball together with a neighborhood of it. Hence ω = Ω \ B does not contain any neighborhood of ∂Ω, Assumption (A3) fails for the defined ω, and the claim 'We choose ω so that Assumption (A3) is satisfied' is false. The subsequent sentence 'we further assume that ω contains the entire boundary ∂Ω' contradicts the just-given definition of ω, so the described configuration is internally inconsistent.
